zh: 他的测度，丝毫不差，胡雪岩正是这样希望。他对俞武成有多少实力，肚子里有些什么货，以及他的想法和脾气。尽皆了然，觉得跟他谈，不如跟杨凤毛谈，来得有用。当然，还有个少不得的人：周一鸣。三个人是在水阁中促膝画策。胡雪岩首先表明了态度，他的目的，已经有所更改，那一船洋枪如何运到杭州，犹在其次，主要的是想帮俞武成翻身，也不枉三婆婆一番器重的情意。江湖上就讲这一点“意思”。杨凤毛对胡雪岩的态度，一变再变，由不甚在意，到相当佩服，而此刻是十分感激了，“胡大叔，”他说了句很坦率的话：“你老的心，我师父或许还不明白，我是完全晓得的。只要胡大叔吩咐，我们做得到的，一定出全力去做。现在胡大叔是这样的用心，我倒想请问一句，照胡大叔看，我师父要怎么样才能翻身？”“官私两面。”胡雪岩很快地回答：“官的，譬如说能够办好这一次招抚，自然最好，不然，就要有杀搏的做法，也是大功一件。”杨凤毛领会得他的意思，一颗心怦怦然，相当紧张，但还不便表示态度，只眼神专注着，等他再说下去。“私的，在江猢上要把你师父的名气，重新打它响来！”“是的。”对这一点，杨凤毛深有同感，“我也一直这样子在想。不过，也要有机会，能够有机会干一两件漂亮的事就好了。”
en: Liu had guessed exactly right: this was precisely what Hu Xueyan wanted. Hu now understood how much real influence Yu Wucheng possessed, what abilities he had, and how he thought and behaved. He felt that a discussion with Yang Fengmao would be more useful than one with Yu. There was, of course, another indispensable participant: Zhou Yiming. The three sat close together in the waterside pavilion to work out a plan. Hu began by explaining his position. His purpose had changed. Getting that boatload of foreign rifles to Hangzhou was now a secondary concern; his chief aim was to help Yu Wucheng regain his standing and thus prove worthy of Third Granny’s regard. In the brotherhood, such a gesture counted for everything. Yang’s feelings toward Hu had changed again and again, from indifference to considerable admiration; now they had become profound gratitude. “Uncle Hu,” he said frankly, “my master may not yet understand what is in your heart, but I understand it completely. Give us your instructions, and whatever we can do, we shall do with all our strength. Since this is what you have in mind, may I ask how you think my master can recover his position?” “On two fronts: with the authorities and within the brotherhood,” Hu answered at once. “As far as the authorities are concerned, successfully arranging this surrender would naturally be best. Failing that, there must be action to put the men down by force. That, too, would be a great service.” Yang understood. His heart began to pound, but he was not yet ready to commit himself. He watched Hu intently, waiting for him to continue. “Within the brotherhood, we must make your master’s name ring out again!” “Exactly.” On this point Yang agreed wholeheartedly. “That is what I have always wanted. But we need an opportunity. If only he could accomplish one or two things that would really impress people!”

zh: “眼前就是个机会。这且摆下来再说。我现在想到一个主意，说出来你看看，行不行？“胡雪岩说：”有句话叫做‘明修栈道，暗渡陈仓’，现在跷脚长根全副精神，都在你师父跟我身上，一双眼睛，只顾看着同里，别的方面就疏忽了。我想趁这个空档，将上海的那船军火，赶紧起运。好在松江那方面有照应，一定不会出毛病。““嗯，嗯！”杨凤毛连连点头，“这个险值得冒。”“不过也有个做法，我想请少武押运。当然，”胡雪岩紧接着说：“万一出了毛病，决不要他负责任。我的意思是，有这样一趟‘劳绩’，等军火到了杭州，奏保议叙，就可以拿他的名字摆在前面，多少有点好处，对三婆婆也是个交代。”“好的。胡大叔挑他，那还有什么话说？等我回苏州去一趟，当面告诉他。”“不必你去，我会安排。”
en: “The opportunity is right before us. But let us put that aside for a moment. An idea has just occurred to me; see what you think of it. There is a saying: ‘Repair the plank road in plain sight, but secretly cross at Chencang.’ Lame Changgen’s whole attention is fixed on your master and me. With both eyes on Tongli, he is neglecting everything else. I want to take advantage of that opening to get the arms shipment out of Shanghai at once. Fortunately, we have people in Songjiang to look after it. Nothing should go wrong.” “Yes, yes!” Yang nodded repeatedly. “That is a risk worth taking.” “But there is another part to it. I should like Shaowu to escort the shipment. Of course,” Hu added quickly, “if anything does go wrong, he will certainly not be held responsible. My idea is that once the arms reach Hangzhou, this service will allow us to put his name near the top when recommendations for rewards are submitted to the throne. It should do him some good, and it will give us something to show Third Granny.” “Excellent. If you have chosen him, Uncle Hu, what more is there to say? I shall go back to Suzhou and tell him myself.” “You need not go. I shall arrange it.”

zh: 接下来便是商量如何对付跷脚长根。胡雪岩与杨凤毛的看法相同，整个关键，就在证据！有了证据，怎么样都好办，大则动用官兵围剿，是师出有名，小则照他们帮里“家门”的规矩，“开香堂”问罪，亦可问得他俯首无辞，三刀六洞，任凭处置。“现在只有这样的消息，既无书信字迹，也没有人肯挺身指证，这就莫亲其何？当然，我也可以想法子拿他抓到公堂上，严刑拷问，不过这一来，我结了怨还在其次，损了你们老头子的威名，说他仗势损人，这个名声，我想他也决不肯背的。”“ 当然，当然。”杨凤毛一叠连声地说，“一落这个名声，在江湖上就难混了。”“所以，除非罢手，不上他的圈套，不然就只有一条路子，叫做‘不入虎穴，焉得虎子’！”“我也想到过，觉得太危险！”“只要接应得好，决不要紧。我想这样子做法……”
en: They next discussed how to deal with Changgen. Hu and Yang agreed that everything depended on evidence. Once they had proof, any course would be open to them. They could call in government troops to surround and suppress his men with full justification; or, on a smaller scale, they could convene an incense-hall tribunal under their own brotherhood’s rules. Confronted with the evidence, he could have no defense and would have to submit to their punishment, even the sentence of “three knife thrusts and six holes.” “At present all we have is this report. There are no letters or written documents, and no one will come forward to testify. What can we do to him? Naturally, I could find a way to have him brought before a magistrate and interrogated under torture. The resentment that would earn me is a minor matter. What matters is the damage to your leader’s reputation: people would say he had used official power to harm another man. I am sure he would never accept that name.” “Certainly not, certainly not,” Yang said repeatedly. “Once a man acquires that reputation, he can scarcely hold his ground in the brotherhood.” “So unless we abandon the matter and keep clear of his trap, there is only one course left: ‘How can you catch the tiger’s cub without entering the tiger’s den?’” “I have thought of that too, but it seemed too dangerous.” “Provided the rescue is properly coordinated, there is no danger. Here is what I propose...”

zh: 胡雪岩的做法是跟俞武成去赴这一场“鸿门宴”，准备谈判决裂，准备被绑架，等船到关卡，借稽查为名，出其不意，上船相救，那时候就证实了跷脚长根的不逞之心，是官了还是私了，到时候再说。杨凤毛极注意地听着，从头到底，细作盘算，认为他的计划，比自己的打算来得周密，前面的一段经过相同，不同的是脱险的方法，杨凤毛预备邀人埋伏，唱一出“临江夺斗”，胡雪岩是动用官方的力量作掩护，围赵救燕。一个力夺，一个智取，自然后者比前者高明。“胡大叔，你老随机应变的功夫，我是信得过的，就怕我师父脾气暴躁，搞得跷脚长根恼羞成怒。除此以外，只要接应得好，不会不成功。”“成败的关键在明暗之间。”胡雪岩说：“跷脚长根以为他在暗处，我们在明处，其实他明我暗。如果消息泄漏出去，就又变成我们在明处了。”“是的。”杨凤毛郑重地答道：“我想，这件事就胡大叔、周先生跟我三个人知道。等筹划好了，再告诉我师父。”“一点不错。”于是彼此不动声色，吃罢了饭，仍旧由刘不才陪着俞武成赌钱，他们三个人接续未完的话题，将一切细节，都筹划到了，然后分头行事。
en: Hu’s plan was to accompany Yu Wucheng to this Banquet at Hongmen, prepared for the negotiations to break down and for both of them to be kidnapped. When their captors’ boat reached a checkpoint, men would board unexpectedly on the pretext of an inspection and rescue them. Changgen’s treachery would then be established. Whether to settle the affair through the authorities or within the brotherhood could be decided afterward. Yang listened closely, working through every stage, and found Hu’s plan more thorough than his own. Their ideas for the first part were the same; the difference lay in the escape. Yang had intended to station men in ambush and stage a rescue like the opera Seizing Adou by the River. Hu would use official authority as cover, “besieging Zhao to save Yan.” One meant a rescue by force, the other by strategy; the latter was plainly superior. “Uncle Hu, I have complete confidence in your ability to meet whatever happens. My only fear is that my master’s violent temper may provoke Changgen into a rage. Apart from that, with the rescue properly arranged, we cannot fail.” “Success depends on who knows what,” Hu replied. “Changgen thinks he is hidden while we stand in the open. In fact, it is he who is exposed and we who are hidden. If word gets out, we shall be the ones exposed again.” “Yes,” Yang said solemnly. “I suggest that only you, Mr Zhou, and I know of this. Once the arrangements are complete, we can tell my master.” “Exactly.” They gave nothing away. After the meal, Liu Bucai again kept Yu company at the gaming table while the three resumed their discussion. When every detail had been settled, they went about their separate tasks.

zh: 首先当然是要告诉俞武成。对于整个计划，他有不以为然的地方，譬如由他儿子去押运那一船洋枪，俞武成就觉得将来说出去，是他先背弃了跷脚长根，名声不好听。但他一向倚人成事，杨凤毛是他最得力的学生，胡雪岩又处处显得比自己这面高明，加以有那一层干亲在，越发不便多说什么。所以慨然答应：“都随你们，你们怎么说，我怎么做！”“有一层要请示大哥，等事情抖明了，是官了，还是私了？”胡雪岩说，“官了，我来奔去，私了，是你们家门里的事，我就不能过问了。”俞武成想了想说：“我想还是私了。惊官动府也不大好。”“那都随大哥的意思，好在我跟大哥始终在一起，有事随时听招呼就是了。”
en: The first task, naturally, was to inform Yu Wucheng. He objected to parts of the plan. Having his own son escort the rifles, for instance, might allow people to say afterward that he had been the first to betray Changgen. That would sound very bad. But he had always relied on others to accomplish things. Yang was his most capable disciple, while Hu had shown himself superior at every turn to anyone on Yu’s side. Their newly established family connection made it still harder to object. He therefore agreed with an expansive air. “I leave it all to you. Whatever you say, I shall do!” “There is one point on which I need your decision, Brother Yu. Once everything has been exposed, shall we settle it officially or privately? If it is to go through the authorities, I shall make the arrangements. If it is to be settled privately, that is a matter for your brotherhood, and I cannot interfere.” Yu considered. “Privately, I think. Bringing in the authorities would not be a good thing.” “Then we shall do as you wish. I shall be with you throughout, in any case, ready to follow your instructions whenever anything arises.”

zh: “始终在一起”这五个字，俞武成深深印入脑中，不由得便有患难祸福相共的感觉，因而对胡雪岩的情分也就不同了。他是豪爽，加上些纨袴子弟想到就做的鲁莽性格，当时便说：“凤毛，你告诉你那些兄弟和‘小角色’，以后胡大叔说的话，就跟我同你说的一样。”“是！”杨凤毛心悦诚服地答道：“我们不敢不敬胡大叔。”“不敢当，不敢当！”胡雪岩既得意，又惭愧，“贤师弟如此厚爱，叫我不知何以为报？”“老胡，你说反了……”“师父！”杨凤毛打断他的话说：“这不是谈这些话的时候。胡大叔还有正事要赶着办，晚上宵夜再谈吧！”
en: The words “with you throughout” sank deep into Yu’s mind. They gave him the sense that here was a man who would share his troubles and good fortune alike, and his feelings toward Hu changed accordingly. He was generous by nature, with something of a spoiled young gentleman’s reckless habit of acting on impulse. “Fengmao,” he said at once, “tell your fellow disciples and all the younger men that from now on Uncle Hu’s word carries exactly the same weight as yours or mine.” “Yes,” Yang answered with willing sincerity. “We would not dare treat Uncle Hu with anything less than respect.” “You are too kind, far too kind!” Hu felt both pleased and abashed. “With such affection from you and your disciple, how can I ever repay you?” “My dear Hu, you have it the wrong way round...” “Master!” Yang interrupted. “This is not the time for that. Uncle Hu still has urgent business to attend to. We can talk over supper tonight.”

zh: 胡雪岩深知江湖上行事，越是光棍，越易多心，过节上的话，要交代得清楚，无端冒出个周一鸣来，已有些自张一帜，独行其是的味道，再藏着个“黑人”裘丰言，再不成话，因而把握机关，作了说明。“有件事，我要跟大哥回明白。老周跟我还有个朋友，也就是那一船洋枪的押运委员裘丰言，他们两位不放心我，现在都赶到同里，预备帮忙。人多好做事，我们调兵遣将，原该在一起，不过，人一多，怕风声太大，我跟大哥请示，是大家住一起，还是分开来的好？”是合是分，俞武成无从作判断，不过听话是听得懂的，胡雪岩既“怕风声太大”，则意向如何？不言可知。于是俞武成毫不迟疑地答道：“分开来的好，分开来的好！”“那位裘大老爷是‘州县班子’，跟刘三爷一样，极有趣的人，三婆婆认胡大婶，算是他引进。”“喔！”俞武成说，“那么，我该尽点道理，明天下个帖子，请裘大老爷吃饭。”“那就不必了。等事情成功了，我们再好好热闹一下子。如果大哥想跟他见一面，我今晚上就把他带了来。”“那好极了！只怕简慢不恭。”
en: Hu knew that in the world of the brotherhood, the more seasoned a man was, the more readily he took offense or grew suspicious. Every point of etiquette had to be made clear. Zhou Yiming had appeared without warning, which already suggested that Hu was setting up a separate camp and acting on his own. To keep Qiu Fengyan hidden as well, another man working in the shadows, would be altogether improper. He therefore took the opportunity to explain. “There is something I must make clear to you, Brother Yu. Zhou and I have another friend, Qiu Fengyan, the officer appointed to escort that shipment of rifles. Both of them were worried about me and have now hurried to Tongli to help. More hands make the work easier. Since we are deploying our people, we ought by rights to be together; but too many of us in one place might attract attention. I should like your opinion: should we all lodge together or remain apart?” Yu had no means of deciding which arrangement was better, but he could understand what he was being told. Since Hu was worried about attracting attention, his own preference was obvious. “Apart would be better, apart would be better!” Yu replied without hesitation. “Mr Qiu belongs to the class of officials eligible for subprefectural and county magistracies. Like Third Master Liu, he is excellent company. It was through him that Third Granny came to take Mrs Hu as a sworn daughter.” “Oh!” said Yu. “Then I must show him some courtesy. I shall send an invitation tomorrow and ask him to dinner.” “That is unnecessary. Once the business is successfully concluded, we can celebrate properly. If you would like to meet him, I can bring him here tonight.” “Excellent! I only hope he will forgive the informality.”

zh: 这样说定了，胡雪岩便由周一鸣陪着去看裘丰言。他正在客栈里，捏着一卷黄仲则的《两当轩全集》，醉眼迷离地在吟哦。一见胡雪岩便即笑道：“老胡，我真服了你！来，来，先奉敬一杯。”“等等，等等，回头消夜，我再陪你吃。如今‘军情紧急’，你先把酒杯放下来。”夺去他的酒杯，自是件极扫兴的事，但他是真的服胡雪岩，说什么是什么，当时便陪着胡雪岩到另一张桌子坐下，细谈正事。胡雪岩将“暗渡陈仓”的计划说了一遍，当时便请他写了三封信，一封是给松江老大，说明经过，请求在水路上照应，一封是由裘丰言自己出面，写给王有龄，说明委任俞少武押运洋枪，作为将来叙功的根据，再一封是写给何桂清，介绍周一鸣晋谒，说有“机密要事”密陈。
en: With that settled, Hu went with Zhou to see Qiu. At the inn they found him holding a volume of Huang Zhongze’s Complete Works of Liangdang Studio, reciting poetry with a tipsy, misty gaze. At the sight of Hu he laughed. “My dear Hu, I truly admire you! Come, come, let me offer you a cup first.” “Wait, wait. I shall drink with you over supper later. For the moment, ‘the military situation is urgent.’ Put down your cup.” To deprive Qiu of his wine was certainly to spoil his pleasure. But his admiration for Hu was genuine, and he accepted whatever Hu said. He joined him at another table to discuss the business in detail. Hu explained the plan for the secret shipment and had Qiu write three letters on the spot. One was to the Songjiang Chief, explaining the circumstances and requesting protection along the waterways. Another, written in Qiu’s own name to Wang Youling, set out Yu Shaowu’s appointment to escort the rifles, providing a record on which a future recommendation for reward could be based. The third introduced Zhou Yiming to He Guiqing, saying that Zhou had confidential matters of importance to report in person.

zh: 写完了信，胡雪岩邀他到朱家消夜，跟俞武成见面。“酒糊涂”的裘丰言，却忽然谨小慎微了，认为做事以隐秘为上，而且他也没有跟俞武成见面的必要。但胡雪岩认为说好了见面，临时变卦，怕俞武成多心，所以坚持原议。这样便不得不有此一行。见了面互道仰慕，而且酒杯中容易交朋友，俞武成觉得此人颇为投机。谈到俞少武押运的差使，做父亲的虽不以为然，而此时竟不能不郑重拜托。这顿消夜，直吃到深夜才罢，裘丰言和周一鸣双双告辞，回到客栈打个盹，上了预先雇定的船，一个往北到苏州去见何桂清，并通知俞少武到上海会齐，一个往东，先到松江见“老太爷”，然后回上海去运洋枪。
en: When the letters were finished, Hu invited Qiu to the Zhu house for supper and a meeting with Yu Wucheng. Qiu, the Wine Muddlehead, suddenly became exceedingly cautious. Secrecy should come first, he argued, and there was no need for him to meet Yu. Hu insisted, however, that since the meeting had already been promised, a last-minute change might arouse Yu’s suspicions. Qiu therefore had to go. The two exchanged expressions of admiration; wine made friendship easy, and Yu found him very congenial. When they spoke of Shaowu’s escort assignment, Yu, though he disapproved of it, now felt obliged to commend his son earnestly to Qiu’s care. Supper lasted far into the night. Qiu and Zhou then took their leave together, returned to the inn for a short nap, and boarded boats hired in advance. One went north to Suzhou, to see He Guiqing and notify Yu Shaowu that he should join the others in Shanghai. The other went east, first to Songjiang to see the Old Master, then back to Shanghai to ship the rifles.

zh: 由于关卡上的安排援救脱险，得有些日子来部署，所以依照预先的商议，先用一条缓兵之计，俞武成向跷脚长根说，胡雪岩为表敬意，坚持要先请他吃饭，从来“行客拜坐客”，但坐客却须先尽地主之谊，因此俞武成提出折中办法，由他作东，先请双方小叙会面，等条件谈妥当了，再领跷脚长根的情。这个说话，合情合理，跷脚长很当然想不到其中别有作用，只觉得自己的计划，晚几天实行，也无所谓，因而欣然应诺。于是就在裘丰言动身的第二天中午，俞武成在朱家设下盛筵，跷脚长根一跷一拐地到了，不知是有意炫耀，还是自觉不甚安全，需人保护，他竟带了二十名随从。这一下，主人家固然手忙脚乱，得要临时添席招待，胡雪岩亦不得不关照刘不才，赶着添办礼物。每人一套衣料，二两银子的一个红包，原来备了八份，此刻需再添十二份。这倒不是他摆阔，是有意笼络，保不定将来遇着性命呼吸的生死关头，有此一重香火因缘，就可能会发生极大的作用。入席谦让，胡雪岩是远客，坐了首座，与跷脚长根接席，在场面上自然都是些冠冕堂皇的应酬话。吃完了饭，刘不才做庄推牌九，以娱“嘉宾”，俞武成则陪着胡雪岩和跷脚长根，到水阁中谈正经，在座的只有一个杨凤毛。
en: Arranging the rescue at the checkpoints would take some days, so they first employed the delaying tactic they had agreed upon. Yu told Changgen that Hu insisted on entertaining him first as a mark of respect. A visitor should always call on the local man, but the local man should first extend hospitality. Yu therefore offered a compromise: he would give a small dinner at which the two sides could meet and talk. Once the terms had been settled, they could accept Changgen’s invitation. This was perfectly reasonable. Changgen suspected no hidden purpose and felt that postponing his own plan for a few days would do no harm. He readily agreed. At noon on the day after Qiu’s departure, Yu held a grand banquet at the Zhu house. Changgen arrived limping, with no fewer than twenty followers. Whether this was a display of importance or a precaution because he felt unsafe, no one could tell. The hosts had to scramble to provide extra tables, while Hu hurriedly told Liu to obtain more gifts. He had prepared eight sets, each consisting of cloth for an outfit and a red packet containing two taels; now twelve more were needed. This was no mere display of wealth. He meant to win the men over. At some future moment when his life hung by a thread, even this slight bond of goodwill might make an enormous difference. After the customary exchange of courtesies over seating, Hu, as the visitor from afar, took the place of honor next to Changgen. The conversation consisted, naturally, of polished pleasantries. Afterward Liu took the bank at pai gow to entertain the “honored guests,” while Yu led Hu and Changgen to the waterside pavilion for serious business. Yang was the only other person present.

zh: “长根！”俞武成先作开场白，“这位胡老兄的如夫人，是我老娘从小就喜欢，认了干亲的，‘大水冲倒龙王庙’，一家人不认识一家人，说起来也是巧事。老胡虽是空子，其实比我们门槛里都还够朋友，他踉松江老大、尤五的交清，是没话说的。还有湖州的郁四，你总也听说过，他们在一伙做生意。所以，那件事，要请你高抬贵手！”“俞师父，你老人家说话太重了，”跷脚长根的态度显得很恳切，“江湖上碰来碰去自己人，光是三婆婆跟你老的面子，我就没话可说。何况，我也很想结交我们胡老兄。”“承情，承情！”胡雪岩拱拱手说：“多蒙情让，我总也要有点意思……”“笑话！”跷脚长根摆着手说，“那件事就不必谈了！”洋枪的事，总算有了交代。于是谈招抚。
en: “Changgen,” Yu began, “my mother has been fond of our friend Hu’s concubine since she was a child, and has taken her as a sworn daughter. It is a case of ‘the flood washing into the Dragon King’s own temple’—members of one family failing to recognize one another. A remarkable coincidence, when you think of it. Hu is not an initiate, but he is a truer friend than many within our ranks. His friendship with the Songjiang Chief and You Laowu needs no explanation. And you must have heard of Yu Si of Huzhou; they are in business together. So I must ask you to show consideration over that matter.” “Master Yu, there is no need to put it so strongly.” Changgen appeared entirely sincere. “We meet people here and there, only to discover that they are our own. Out of respect for Third Granny and yourself alone, I could have nothing more to say. Besides, I very much want to make our friend Hu’s acquaintance.” “I am grateful, very grateful!” Hu clasped his hands. “Since you are being so accommodating, I must make some gesture in return...” “Nonsense!” Changgen waved this aside. “There is no need to discuss that matter again!” The question of the rifles had at last been addressed. They turned to the proposed surrender.

zh: 跷脚长根亦颇会做作，明明并无就抚之心，却在条件上斤斤较量，反复争论，显得极其认真似地，特别是对改编为官军以后的驻区，坚持要在嘉定、昆山和青浦这个三角形的地带上。一直是胡雪岩耐着性子跟他磨，到了僵持不下之时，俞武成忍不住要开口，“长根！”他用低沉的声音说：“做事总要‘前半夜想想自己，后半夜想想别人’。我倒要问你一句：等招安以后，上头要派你出队去打上海县城，你肯不肯去？”“这……俞师父，你晓得我的处境的。”“是啊！”俞武成紧接着他的话说，“别人也就是晓得你的处境，不肯叫你为难，所以要把你调开。不然的话，你跟小刀会倒还有香火之情，小刀会不见得跟你请义气，冷不防要来吃掉你，那时候你怎么办？老实说一句：你想退让都办不到！为什么呢，一则，你当官军，小刀会就不当你朋友了，说不定赶尽杀绝，再则，你一退就动摇军心，军令如山，父子部不认帐的，‘辕门斩子’这出戏，你难道没有看过？”
en: Changgen was an accomplished actor. He had no intention of surrendering, yet he haggled over every condition and argued back and forth as though he were perfectly serious. Above all, he insisted that once his men were incorporated into the government army, they must remain stationed in the triangle formed by Jiading, Kunshan, and Qingpu. Hu patiently argued with him until they reached an impasse. Then Yu could contain himself no longer. “Changgen,” he said in a low voice, “when you do anything, you should ‘think of yourself for the first half of the night, and of others for the second.’ Let me ask you this: once you have accepted the amnesty, if your superiors order you to attack the county town of Shanghai, will you go?” “Well... Master Yu, you know my position.” “Exactly!” Yu seized on his reply. “And it is because other people understand your position and do not want to put you in a difficulty that they intend to move you elsewhere. Otherwise, you may still feel a bond with the Small Swords Society, but they may not feel any obligation to you. Suppose they suddenly try to swallow you up. What will you do then? To be frank, you would not even be free to give way. Why? First, once you become government troops, the Small Swords will no longer regard you as friends; they may even try to wipe you out. Second, if you retreat, you shake the army’s morale. Military orders are immovable as a mountain; they make no allowance even for fathers and sons. Surely you have seen the opera Executing the Son at the Camp Gate?”

zh: 跷脚长根被驳倒了，沉吟了好半晌，做出情恳的神态，“俞师父，胡老兄，我实在有我的难处，弟兄们一份饷只好混自己，养家活口是不够的，在本乡本土，多少有点生路，一调开了，顾不到家眷，没有一个人安得下心来。俞师父你老的话，当然再透彻都没有，我就听凭上头作主，不过‘皇帝不差饿兵’，请上头无论如何发半年的恩饷，算是安家费。家不安，心不定，出队打仗也不肯拼命的，胡老兄，你说是不是？““是，是。你老兄再明白不过。”胡雪岩很诚恳地说，“我一定替你去力争。半年，恐怕不大办得到，三个月，我一定替你争来。能多自然最好。”“好了，好了！话说到这里，长根，你要再争就不够意思了！”“是的。”跷脚长根略带些勉强地，仿佛是因为俞武成以大压小，不敢不听，“我就听你老的吩咐了。”“好极！总算谈出个结果。”胡雪岩看着俞武成说：“大哥，我想明天就回苏州。官场上做事慢，恐怕要五、六天才谈得好。不过，到底有多少人马，要有个确数，上头才好筹划。”这是想跟跷脚长根要本花名册，俞武成虽懂得他的意思，却感到有些不易措词，怕跷脚长根托词拒绝，碰一个钉子，则以自己的身分，面子上下不来。
en: Unable to answer this, Changgen brooded for some time, then assumed an earnest expression. “Master Yu, my dear Hu, I really do have difficulties. The men’s pay is barely enough to keep them alive; it will not support their families. At home they have other ways of making a little money. If they are transferred and cannot look after their dependents, none of them will have any peace of mind. What you say, Master Yu, could not be clearer, and I shall leave the decision to the authorities. But ‘even the emperor does not send hungry soldiers into the field.’ Whatever happens, I must ask them to grant six months’ bonus pay to provide for the men’s families. If their homes are unsettled, their minds will be unsettled, and they will not fight with all their strength. Am I not right, my dear Hu?” “Yes, yes. You understand the situation perfectly.” Hu spoke with great sincerity. “I shall certainly press your case. Six months may be difficult, but I promise to obtain three. More would naturally be better.” “Enough, enough! We have got this far, Changgen. It would be unreasonable to keep arguing!” “Very well.” Changgen appeared a little reluctant, as though Yu were invoking his seniority and he dared not disobey. “I shall do as you say.” “Excellent! At last we have reached an agreement.” Hu turned to Yu. “Brother Yu, I should like to return to Suzhou tomorrow. Official business moves slowly; settling this may take five or six days. But we need exact figures for the men and horses, so the authorities can make their plans.” He wanted Changgen’s muster roll. Yu understood, but found the request difficult to frame. If Changgen made an excuse and refused, a man of Yu’s standing would suffer an intolerable loss of face.

zh: 谁知跷脚长根倒爽快得很，不待俞武成开口，自己就说：“对，对！”接着便喊一声：“贵生！”贵生是他的一名随从，生得雄武非常，腰里别一把短枪，枪上一绺猩红丝穗子，昂然走了进来候命。“你把我那个‘护书’拿来。”取来“护书”，跷脚长根从里面抽出一张纸来，递给胡雪岩，打开一看，上面记得有数字：两千七百人，三百五十匹马，此外记着武器的数目，如长枪、大刀、白蜡杆子，另外还有四十多支洋枪。胡雪岩虽不曾经手过招抚的事务，但平时跟王有龄、嵇鹤龄、裘丰言闭谈之中，已略知其中的关键虚实，大致盗匪就抚，老老实实陈报实力的，例子极少，不是虚增，就是暗减。而就在这增减之中，可以看出受抚者的态度，如果有心受抚，自然希望受到重视，所以人马总是多报些，用虚张声势来自高身价，倘或一时势穷力蹙，不得不暂时投降，暂保生路，那就一定有所隐瞒，作为保存实力，俟机翻复的退步。胡雪岩现在想探明的，就是跷脚长根真正的实力。
en: Unexpectedly, Changgen was most accommodating. Before Yu could speak, he said, “Quite right, quite right!” Then he called, “Guisheng!” One of his followers, a remarkably powerful-looking man, strode proudly in to receive his orders. A pistol hung at his waist, decorated with a scarlet silk tassel. “Bring me my document wallet.” When it arrived, Changgen took out a sheet of paper and handed it to Hu. It listed 2,700 men and 350 horses, followed by the quantities of their weapons: long spears, broadswords, white-waxwood staves, and more than forty foreign rifles. Hu had never personally handled a negotiated surrender, but conversations with Wang Youling, Ji Heling, and Qiu had given him some understanding of how to distinguish appearance from reality in such affairs. Very few bandit leaders reported their strength honestly. They either inflated it or concealed part of it, and the direction of the discrepancy revealed their intentions. A man sincerely wishing to surrender wanted to be taken seriously, so he exaggerated his men and horses to increase his bargaining value. A man driven by desperation to surrender temporarily merely to survive would conceal some of his forces, preserving strength for a later change of sides. What Hu now wanted to discover was Changgen’s actual strength.

zh: “老兄诚意相待，让我中间人毫不为难，实在心感之至。现在有句话想请教，我回到苏州，是不是拿老兄的这张单子，送了上去？”这意思是说，单子送了上来，即是备了案，“一字入公门，九牛拔不转”，将来就抚时，便得照单点验。他这样试探，就是要看看跷脚长根的态度，倘或有心就抚，听此一说，自然要郑重考虑，否则，便不当回事了。果然，胡雪岩试探出来了，“尽管送上去！”跷脚长根答道，“将来照这单子点数，我可以写包票，一个人不少，一匹马不缺。”越是说得斩钉截铁，越显得是假话，因为天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福，这两千七百多人中，难免没有暴疾而亡的事情发生，何能包得下一个不少？他的心思深，跷脚长根和俞武成都想不到有这样的用意在内，只觉得事情谈到此，可以告一段落，当时约定，等他从苏州回来那天，便是在妙珍香闺畅饮庆功之日。
en: “You have dealt so frankly with me that my work as intermediary could not be easier. I am deeply grateful. There is just one thing I should like to ask: when I return to Suzhou, may I submit this list of yours to the authorities?” Submission meant that the list would become an official record. “Once a word enters a government office, nine oxen cannot pull it back”: when Changgen surrendered, his men and horses would have to be inspected and counted against it. Hu was testing his attitude. Anyone seriously contemplating surrender would consider this carefully; anyone who was not would attach no importance to it. The test produced its answer. “Submit it by all means!” Changgen replied. “When the time comes, they can count according to that list. I will give you a written guarantee: not a man short, not a horse missing.” The more emphatic he was, the less credible his words became. Misfortune could arrive without warning. Among 2,700 men, someone might suddenly fall ill and die. How could he guarantee that not one would be missing? Hu’s thinking ran too deep for either Changgen or Yu to suspect his purpose. They merely felt that the discussion had reached a suitable stopping point, and agreed that on the day Hu returned from Suzhou they would drink to their success in Miaozhen’s chambers.

zh: 谈完正事，少不得有点余兴，这时在大厅上的赌，已经由一桌变成两桌，一桌牌九一桌摊，另外在厢房里有两桌麻将。俞武成陪着跷脚长根来做庄，胡雪岩反对，认为庄家赢了钱该继续往下推，让下风有个翻本的机会。刘不才这一阵子跟胡雪岩朝夕相处，默契更深，听他这一说，立即会意，当时便改了宗旨，不以赢钱为目的。赌钱想赢不容易，想输不难，不过刘不才就是输钱，也要使点手段，潜注默察，哪个大输，哪个小赢，一一了然于胸，然后运用大牌九配牌的巧妙，斟酌情形，该放的放，该紧的紧，调剂盈虚，很快地使得十之七八都番本出了赢钱。自己结一结帐，输了三千银子，便笑嘻嘻地站起身“推位让国”。这三千银子输得跷脚长根的手下，皆大欢喜，一致称赞他是第一等的赌客。接下来跷脚长根推庄，照规矩，他一个做头脑的，跟他手下赌，必得送几文，一千银子很快地输光。胡雪岩想输些钱给他，却不知怎么样才输得掉？
en: After business, some entertainment was in order. The gaming in the main hall had expanded from one table to two: pai gow at one and the dice-shaking game at the other. There were also two mahjong tables in the side rooms. Yu accompanied Changgen over to take the bank, but Hu objected. The banker had won money, he said, and ought to continue so that the other players had a chance to recover their losses. Living in Hu’s company day and night had deepened Liu’s understanding of him. He caught the meaning at once and changed his objective: he would no longer try to win. Winning at gambling is difficult; losing is easy. But even when losing, Liu employed some skill. By unobtrusive observation he knew exactly who had lost heavily and who had won a little. Using the possibilities for arranging hands in the full version of pai gow, he eased up or held firm as appropriate, redistributing the gains and losses. Before long, seven or eight players out of ten had recovered their stakes and were showing a profit. Liu reckoned his own loss at three thousand taels, then rose with a smile and “abdicated his throne.” His loss left Changgen’s followers delighted; all declared him a gambler of the first order. Changgen took the bank next. Custom required a leader playing against his followers to let them win something, and he soon lost a thousand taels. Hu wanted to lose some money to him, but could not see how to manage it.

zh: “怎么！”跷脚长根不明他的用意，看着胡雪岩问道：“不下手玩玩？”“我对此道外行。”胡雪岩微笑着答道，“再看一看！”跷脚长根不知是忽发豪兴，还是别有作用，突然间提高了声音，看着胡雪岩说道：“老兄，我们赌一记，怎么样？”“好！”胡雪岩答得也很爽脆，“奉陪。”然后又问：“是不是对赌？”对赌就没有庄家、下风之分，跷脚长根在场面上也很漂亮，很快地答道：“自然是对赌，两不吃亏。怎么赌法，你说！”所谓“怎么赌法”是问赌多少银子，胡雪岩有意答非所问地说：“赌一颗真心！”这话出口，旁人的眼光都不约而同地看一看胡雪岩，再看跷脚长根，只见他一愣，双眼不住眨着，仿佛深感困惑似地，接着笑容满面地答道：“对，对！赌一颗真心！老兄，我不会输给你。”这意思是他亦有一颗真心，然而这话也在可信、可疑之间，借机喻意，当不得真，胡雪岩自己把话拉了转来：“我是说笑话。你我连俞大哥在内，待朋友啊个不是真心。何用再赌？来，来！赌钱，赌钱！”他看着刘不才说，“三爷，借一万银子给我。”
en: “Well?” Changgen asked, unaware of Hu’s intention. “Aren’t you going to try your hand?” “I am a novice at this,” Hu replied with a smile. “Let me watch a little longer.” Whether from a sudden burst of enthusiasm or some other motive, Changgen abruptly raised his voice. “My dear Hu, how about a wager between the two of us?” “Certainly!” Hu answered just as readily. “I shall be happy to oblige. You mean head to head?” In such a game there was no distinction between banker and ordinary player. Changgen knew how to make a handsome gesture in public. “Naturally! Neither of us will have an advantage. What shall we stake? You decide.” He meant how much money, but Hu deliberately answered a different question. “A sincere heart!” Everyone looked from Hu to Changgen. Changgen paused, blinking as though deeply puzzled, then broke into a broad smile. “Yes, yes! A sincere heart! My dear friend, I shall not lose to you.” He meant that his own heart was sincere too, though the claim might be true or false. It was a figurative declaration prompted by the occasion and could not be taken literally. Hu brought the conversation back. “I was joking. You, I, Brother Yu—which of us is anything but sincere with our friends? Why wager on that? Come, let us play for money!” He turned to Liu. “Third Master, lend me ten thousand taels.”

zh: 等刘不才数了一万两的银票，交了过去，胡雪岩顺手就摆在天门上。于是跷脚长根又叫贵主把那个护书拿来，朝桌子中间一放，表示等见了输赢再结算，但在赌场中，这是个狂傲的举动，有着以大压小的意味，俞武成看着很不舒服，忍不住就说了句：“我也赌一记！”真所谓“光棍一点就透”，跷脚长根赶紧一面伸手去取护书，一面赔笑说道：“俞师父出于，我就不敢接了。回头你老人家推几方给我们来打。”这是打俞武成的招呼，自是一笑置之，跷脚长根也不敢再有什么出格的花佯，规规矩矩理了一叠银票，放在手边，然后问道：“赌大的，还是小的？”“小的爽快！”跷脚长根便将副乌木牌九，一阵乱抹，随手捡了两副，拿起骰子说道：“单进双出。”骰子撒出去，打了个五点，这是单进，他把外面的那副牌收进来，顺手一翻，真正“两瞪眼”了！是个蹩十。
en: Liu counted out ten thousand taels in banknotes and handed them over. Hu laid them at the Heaven Gate position on the table. Changgen called for Guisheng to bring his document wallet again, then placed it in the middle, indicating that he would settle after the result was known. At a gaming table this was an arrogant gesture, implying a right to impose on someone of lesser standing. Yu found it offensive. “I shall have a wager too!” he said. A seasoned man needed no more than a hint. Changgen immediately reached for the wallet, saying with an apologetic smile, “If Master Yu is playing, I should not dare accept the wager. Later, you must take the bank for a few rounds and let us play against you.” It was an acknowledgment of Yu’s rebuke, and Yu let it pass with a smile. Changgen ventured no further liberties. He properly laid a stack of banknotes beside him, then asked, “The full game or the small one?” “The small one is quicker!” Changgen shuffled the ebony pai gow tiles, picked out two hands, and took up the dice. “Odd comes in, even goes out.” He threw a five. Since that meant the outer hand came in, he drew it toward himself and turned it over. His eyes widened in dismay: a dead ten!

zh: 胡雪岩不想赢他这一万银子。他的赌不精，对赌徒的心情却很了解，有时输钱是小事，一口气输不起。特别是跷脚长根此时的境况，不用打听，就可以猜想得到，势穷力蹙，已到了铤而走险的地步，一万银子究竟不是小数目，一名兵勇的饷银是一两五钱到二两银子，他手下二千七百人，如果改编为官军，发三个月的恩饷，还不到一万银子，就这样一举手之间输掉了，替他想想，心里也不是味道！有钱输倒还罢了，看样子是输不起的，一输就更得动歪脑筋，等于逼他“上梁山”。这样电闪一般转着念头，手下就极快，当大家还为跷脚长根错愕嗟叹之际，他已把两张牌，抢到了手里。场面上是胡雪岩占尽了优势，跷脚长根已经认输，将那一万银票推到了他的面前，脸色自不免有些尴尬。其余的人则都将视线集中在胡雪岩的两张牌上，心急的人，并且喊道：“先翻一张！”胡雪岩正拇指在上，中指在下，慢慢摸着牌，感觉再迟钝的人也摸得出来，是张地牌，这张牌决不能翻，因为一翻就赢定了跷脚长根。他决计不理旁人的怂勇关切，只管自己做作，摸到第二张牌，先是一怔，然后皱眉，继之以摇头，将两张牌，往未理的乱牌中一推，顺手收回了自己的银票。
en: Hu did not want to win those ten thousand taels. He was no expert gambler, but he understood gamblers’ feelings. Sometimes the money was a small matter; it was the humiliation they could not bear. Changgen’s present circumstances were especially easy to guess. He was so hard pressed that he was ready to take desperate risks. Ten thousand taels was no small sum. A soldier’s pay was between one and a half and two taels; even three months’ bonus pay for his 2,700 men, if they joined the government army, would come to less than ten thousand taels. To lose it all in a single turn of the hand—Hu felt uncomfortable merely imagining it. If Changgen could afford the loss, that would be one thing. But he plainly could not. Losing would only drive him toward more desperate schemes, as though he were being forced to “take to Liangshan” as an outlaw. These thoughts flashed through Hu’s mind, and his hands moved just as quickly. While everyone else was still staring and sighing over Changgen’s bad luck, he seized his own two tiles. Everything favored Hu. Changgen had already conceded defeat and pushed his ten thousand taels in notes across, looking decidedly embarrassed. The others all watched Hu’s tiles, and the impatient ones called, “Turn one over first!” With thumb above and middle finger below, Hu slowly felt a tile. Even the least sensitive fingers could have identified it: an Earth tile. He must not expose it, for the moment he did, his victory over Changgen would be certain. Ignoring the spectators’ encouragement and concern, he continued his performance. At the second tile he started, frowned, then shook his head. He pushed both tiles back into the unarranged heap and casually retrieved his own banknotes.

zh: “怎么样？”跷脚长根一面问，一面取了张胡雪岩的牌去摸。“丁七蹩！”胡雪岩懒懒地答道：“和气！”怎会是“丁七瞥”？跷脚长根不信，细细从中指的感觉上去分辨，明明是张“二六”，有这张牌就决没有“蹩十”，再取另外一张来摸，才知道十点倒也是十点，只不过是一副地罡。“难得和气！”他说：“和气最好！赌过了，好朋友只好赌一次，不好赌第二次。谢谢俞师父了，叨扰，叨扰！”“时候还早嘛！再玩一息？”“不玩了。”跷脚长根答道：“相聚的日子还长。等胡老兄从苏州回来，我们再叙，”
en: “What have you got?” Changgen asked, picking up one of Hu’s tiles and feeling it. “Ding-seven, a dead ten,” Hu answered languidly. “An amicable draw!” How could it be ding-seven? Changgen did not believe him. His middle finger carefully traced what was unmistakably a “two-six” tile; with that tile, the hand could not be a dead ten. He felt the other and understood. The total was indeed ten, but the combination was an Earth Gang. “An amicable result is a rare pleasure!” he said. “Harmony is best. We have had our wager. Good friends should play against each other once, never twice. Thank you for your hospitality, Master Yu!” “But it is still early. Won’t you stay a little longer?” “No more gambling,” Changgen replied. “We shall have plenty of time together. When our friend Hu returns from Suzhou, we can meet again.”

zh: 等他一走，俞武成悄悄问胡雪岩：“你到底是副什么牌，我不相信你连蹩十都吃不了它！”“是副地罡。”胡雪岩说，“我看他的境况也不大好，于心不忍。”“你倒真舍得！铜钱掼在水里还听个响声，你一万两银子就这样阴干了？”其词若有憾焉，其实是故意这样讥嘲，胡雪岩一时辨不清他的意思，唯有报之以一笑。“老胡，怪不得我老娘都佩服你！”俞武成这时才说了他的想法，“现在，你交情是放出去了！要看跷脚是人，还是畜生？是人，当然不会做出什么狗屁倒灶的事，是畜生，我们就当他一条毒蛇打，要打在七寸上！死不足惜。““我就是这个意思。”胡雪岩说，“这一来，我们就是下了辣手，只怪他自己不好，不但我们自己心里不会难过，就是有人替他出头，‘四方台子八方理’，我们也可以把话摆在台面上来讲。”“一点都不错！你对江湖上的过节，熟透，真不晓得你是哪里学来的？”胡雪岩笑笑答道：“闲话少说，我明天一早就走，大概三、五天就回来。这里都拜托大哥了。“
en: After he left, Yu asked Hu quietly, “What hand did you really have? I cannot believe you failed to beat a dead ten.” “An Earth Gang. His circumstances did not seem good, and I could not bring myself to take his money.” “You certainly know how to part with money! Throw a copper coin into water and you at least hear a splash. Your ten thousand taels have simply dried up without a sound!” His words suggested regret, but he was deliberately teasing. Hu could not immediately tell what he meant and could only smile. “My dear Hu, no wonder even my mother admires you!” Yu now explained his thinking. “You have extended your friendship. We shall see whether the cripple is a man or a beast. If he is a man, he will not do anything foul. If he is a beast, we shall treat him as a venomous snake and strike straight at its vital spot. His death would be no loss.” “Exactly my intention,” Hu replied. “If we have to act harshly now, he will have only himself to blame. Not only shall we have easy consciences; even if someone comes forward on his behalf, there are reasons to be heard on every side of the table, and we can put ours before everyone.” “Quite right! You know every nicety of brotherhood conduct. I cannot imagine where you learned it all.” Hu smiled. “Enough of that. I shall leave early tomorrow and should be back in three to five days. Everything here is in your hands, Brother Yu.”

zh: 第五天上，胡雪岩如他自己所预定的期限，回到了同里，周一鸣是跟他一起来的。一到便调兵遣将，周一鸣和杨凤毛守住运河两头的卡子，朱老大打接应，刘不才串清客，陪着胡雪岩和俞武成去赴那场“鸿门宴”。等布置停当，跷脚长根的帖子也送到了，日期是在两天以后，所以不一到就请，理由是妙珍家的厨子，整治一桌水陆杂陈的盛宴，需要两天的工夫。当然，谈正事归谈正事，送帖子的当天，跷脚长根专诚来讨消息。跷脚长根随身带一个蓝布包裹，不知包着什么东西？客人不说。主人也不便问，说过几句闲话，随即问起此行的结果。“四个月的恩饷……”四个月的恩饷，跷脚长根可以保为四品的武官，驻区此刻不能预定，但一定会周到他处。胡雪岩说了这三个主要条件，留视观察跷脚长根的态度，倒要看看他用些什么话来敷衍。
en: On the fifth day, within the time he had set himself, Hu returned to Tongli with Zhou Yiming. They began deploying their people at once. Zhou and Yang were to hold the checkpoints at the two ends of the canal, Eldest Brother Zhu would provide support, and Liu would play the part of a convivial guest, accompanying Hu and Yu to their Banquet at Hongmen. Once everything was arranged, Changgen’s invitation arrived. The dinner was set for two days later. The reason for the delay, rather than entertaining Hu immediately on his return, was that Miaozhen’s cook needed two days to prepare a lavish feast of delicacies from land and water. Business, of course, still had to be discussed separately. On the day the invitation was delivered, Changgen came in person to ask for news. He brought a blue cloth bundle. What it contained was a mystery; since the guest said nothing, the hosts could hardly ask. After a few pleasantries, he inquired about the results of Hu’s journey. “Four months’ bonus pay...” Hu set out the three principal terms: four months’ bonus pay; the possibility of recommending Changgen for a fourth-rank military appointment; and a posting still to be determined, but certainly outside his present area. He watched Changgen closely, curious to see what evasions he would offer.

zh: “既然要投过来，好坏都说不得了。有你老兄在，决不会叫我们弟兄吃亏，我就谨遵台命了。”说着，跷脚长根亲自解开蓝布包裹，里面是一叠旧簿子，封面上写着四个大字：“同心一德”。“这是花名册。我就只有这一份，时间局促，来不及誊清，只好请你看底册了。”胡雪岩和俞武成相顾愕然，竟不知跷脚长根是何用意？看那册子，油腻垢污，拿在手里部有些厌恶，翻开来看，里面涂涂改改，有些地方注一个“逃”字，有些地方注一个“亡”字，有些地方注着“改归某队”，是真实不虚的底册。
en: “If we are going to come over, we cannot keep complaining about the terms. With you there, my dear friend, our men will never be allowed to suffer. I shall do as you say.” Changgen untied the blue cloth himself. Inside was a stack of old registers, their covers bearing the words “One Heart, One Purpose.” “These are the muster rolls. I have only this one set. There was no time to have a fair copy made, so I must ask you to look at the originals.” Hu and Yu exchanged astonished glances, unable to understand his intention. The books were greasy and grimy, unpleasant even to hold. Inside, the entries were covered in alterations and corrections. Some were marked “deserted,” some “dead,” and others “transferred to such-and-such a unit.” These were genuine working registers.

zh: “好极，好极！”胡雪岩只好当他确有诚意，“这份底册，我借用两天，请几个人分开来赶抄。”“不用你老兄费心，里面有些变动的情形，别人弄不清楚，我派人来抄。不过，“跷脚长根看着朱老大说，”我预备派三个人来，要在府上打扰两天。“这好象是更进一步表现了诚意，当朱家是他自己办机密事务的地方。俞武成不等主人开口，便代为应允：“小事，小事！尽管请过来。”“谢谢！就这样说了。今天我还有点事，不打搅了，后天下午，早点请过来，还有许多事要请教。”
en: “Excellent, excellent!” Hu could only treat this as evidence of real sincerity. “Let me borrow these originals for two days. I shall divide them among several people and have them copied quickly.” “There is no need to trouble yourself. Other people would not understand some of the changes. I shall send my own men to copy them. But,” Changgen added, turning to Eldest Brother Zhu, “I intend to send three men. They will have to impose on your hospitality for two days.” This seemed a further demonstration of good faith, treating the Zhu house as a place where he could transact confidential business. Before the host could answer, Yu agreed for him. “A small matter, a small matter! Send them over by all means.” “Thank you! Then it is settled. I have something else to attend to today, so I shall not keep you. Please come early in the afternoon the day after tomorrow. There are still many things on which I want your advice.”

zh: 等跷脚长根一走，胡雪岩大为紧张，也大为兴奋，将俞武成拉到一边，悄悄问道：“大哥，你看怎么样？这家伙，不象是耍花样？”“是啊！我也有点想不懂。他把底册都拿了来了，竟象是真有这回事！我想，“俞武成说：”不如托老周再去摸一摸底看。““对！”于是，周一鸣受命去打听跷脚长根的真实意向，如果真的愿意就抚，则前后的态度大不相同，何以有此突然的大变化？要找出能够令人满意的解释来，方可以使人信其为真。周一鸣的消息不曾来，苏州却有了信息，何桂清用专差送了一封信给胡雪岩，说是由江苏营务处得来的消息，青浦、嘉定之间，不断有一股一股的“匪徒”在移动，携带武器，行迹诡秘，自称是由各地集中，听候官方点验。深怕这是借机蠢动，请胡雪岩赶紧打探明白，是不是确有其事。如果并无其事，则将出动清军兜剿。信尾特别赘了一句：“此事关系重大，务望火速回示。”
en: Once Changgen had gone, Hu felt both deeply anxious and greatly excited. Drawing Yu aside, he asked quietly, “What do you think, Brother Yu? The fellow does not seem to be playing tricks.” “Yes, I cannot quite understand it either. He has even brought the original registers. It almost looks as though he means it! I think we should ask Zhou to investigate again.” “Quite right!” Zhou was accordingly sent to discover Changgen’s real intentions. If he genuinely wished to surrender, his attitude had changed completely. What could account for such a sudden reversal? They needed a convincing explanation before they could believe it. Before Zhou’s report arrived, however, news came from Suzhou. He Guiqing sent Hu a letter by special messenger. The Jiangsu Military Affairs Office had reported that armed bands of “bandits” were continually moving between Qingpu and Jiading, behaving furtively and claiming that they were gathering from various places to await an official inspection. He feared that they were using this pretext to stir up trouble and urged Hu to find out at once whether there really was such a gathering for surrender. If there was not, Qing troops would be sent to surround and suppress them. At the end of the letter he added a special injunction: “This matter is of great consequence. I earnestly request an immediate reply.”
